how_work.111: Quick answers to common questions about the boilerplate.
how_work.112: Can I use this for commercial projects?
how_work.113: Yes! The boilerplate is MIT licensed. You can use it commercially, modify it, distribute it, and even sell products built with it without any attribution requirements.
how_work.115: Rust 1.75+ (stable). We track the latest stable Rust release and update the MSRV (Minimum Supported Rust Version) conservatively.
how_work.116: Can I use a different database?
how_work.117: Diesel supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite. The boilerplate uses PostgreSQL by default but can be adapted. Diesel's query builder abstracts most differences.
how_work.119: JWT access tokens (short-lived) + refresh tokens (long-lived, revocable). Paseto for email verification. Argon2id for password hashing. Optional TOTP 2FA. OAuth2 providers can be added via the auth service.
how_work.120: Can I remove features I don't need?
how_work.121: Absolutely. The modular architecture makes it easy to remove unused modules (e.g., WebSocket server, admin panel, specific API routes) without affecting the core.
how_work.122: How do I deploy to production?
how_work.123: Use the provided Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests. The multi-stage Dockerfile creates minimal images. Health checks, graceful shutdown, and env-based config are built-in.
how_work.124: Is there a migration guide from v0.x?
how_work.125: Yes, see the MIGRATION.md file in the repository. The v1.0 release includes breaking changes for improved architecture, but we provide step-by-step upgrade instructions.
how_work.127: We welcome contributions! See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. Areas: bug fixes, new features, documentation, translations, security audits, and testing improvements.
how_work.129: Clone the repository, follow the quick start guide, and have a running full-stack application in minutes.

contact.2: We'd Love to Hear from You
contact.3: Have questions about the boilerplate? Need enterprise support? Want to contribute? Our team is here to help.

contact.32: Quick answers to common questions about the boilerplate.
contact.34: Yes! The boilerplate includes authentication, authorization, admin panel, database migrations, Docker setup, and comprehensive tests. It's designed for production use from day one.
contact.35: Can I use this for commercial projects?
contact.36: Absolutely! The project is MIT licensed, which permits commercial use, modification, distribution, and private use without attribution requirements.
contact.38: Community support is available via GitHub Discussions and Discord. For enterprise customers, we offer dedicated support channels with SLA guarantees and priority response times.
contact.39: Does it work with my existing database?
contact.40: Yes! The boilerplate uses Diesel ORM with PostgreSQL. You can connect to any PostgreSQL-compatible database (AWS RDS, Supabase, Neon, Cloud SQL, etc.) by updating the DATABASE_URL environment variable.
contact.41: Can I remove features I don't need?
contact.42: Yes! The modular architecture makes it easy to remove unused modules. Each feature (auth, admin, websockets, etc.) is isolated. Simply remove the routes, controllers, and dependencies you don't need.
contact.44: The boilerplate includes Docker multi-stage builds and docker-compose for local development. For production, deploy the Docker images to any container platform (Kubernetes, ECS, Cloud Run, Fly.io, Railway, etc.). Health checks and graceful shutdown are built-in.
contact.46: Dedicated support, custom feature development, security audits, migration assistance, and SLA-backed response times.
